trustedProxies.label: Trusted proxies
trustedProxies.description: Empty trusts only Cloudflare. Behind a local reverse proxy / Docker, set the proxy's subnet so logs and rate limiting use the real client IP

anthropicAutoCacheControl.label: Auto cache (Claude)
anthropicAutoCacheControl.description: Marks long prompts and earlier turns for caching, so resending is faster and cheaper. Skipped if the client marked any.
anthropicAutoCacheControl.hint:
Anthropic channels only, and only when the request has no cache markers.
Marks the start (system / tools / first message) if long enough, plus the last two user messages.
Too short: nothing added. Real Claude Code marks its own and is left alone.

openAIAutoPromptCacheKey.label: Auto cache (OpenAI)
openAIAutoPromptCacheKey.description: Lets the upstream reuse a long repeated conversation start: faster and cheaper. Skipped if the client set its own.
openAIAutoPromptCacheKey.hint:
OpenAI Chat / Responses channels only.
Builds a cache ID from user, model and conversation start; only a hash is sent, never the text.
Real Codex sends its own ID and is left alone.

headerDefaults.title: Header Defaults
headerDefaults.hint: Filled only when the upstream request is missing these client identity headers. Channel custom headers still override them.
headerDefaults.description: Claude applies to Anthropic channels. Codex applies to OpenAI Responses channels.
headerDefaults.claudeDescription: For Anthropic channels: Claude CLI identity headers and thinking settings.
headerDefaults.codexDescription: For OpenAI Responses channels: Codex identity headers, speed and thinking settings.

claudeCLIReasoningEffort.label: Default thinking effort
claudeCLIReasoningEffort.description: Used when the client does not pick one. A client's own choice is never changed.
claudeCLIReasoningEffort.hint:
Non-Claude-Code clients only; real Claude Code is left alone.
Steps down if the model lacks the level; skipped on older models, with temperature-style sampling, or a forced tool call.
Higher is slower and uses more.

claudeBetaStripFlags.label: Claude Beta strip flags
claudeBetaStripFlags.hint: When empty, the downstream claude-cli's anthropic-beta is forwarded verbatim (default, zero behaviour change). Set a comma-separated list of beta flags to strip them from the outbound anthropic-beta — an escape hatch for when an upstream throws a 520 on a specific flag, while the rest of the genuine shape is preserved.
claudeBetaStripFlags.description: Upstream escape hatch: comma-separated, empty = off. e.g. prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05.

codexFastMode.label: Codex fast mode
codexFastMode.description: Asks the upstream to serve you first: faster replies, usually about 2x the price. Skipped if the client chose.
codexFastMode.hint:
Adds service_tier=priority when the client sent no service tier.
Leave off if the upstream does not support it. Does not lower thinking effort.

streamKeepalive.label: Stream keepalive interval
streamKeepalive.hint: Sends a keepalive only during an active streaming request when no output has been written for the configured number of seconds. It does not start another upstream request or consume extra tokens.
streamKeepalive.description: Helps long Claude/MCP tool calls survive reverse proxies and clients that close apparently idle streams.
streamKeepalive.envHint: can still provide the first deployment default.
streamKeepalive.invalid: Keepalive interval must be 0 or a positive integer number of seconds

firstByteKeepalive.label: First-byte keepalive delay
firstByteKeepalive.hint: When a streaming request waits longer than this many seconds for the upstream first byte, octopus injects a keepalive comment downstream to prevent idle-connection cuts by a front-end reverse proxy. Only enable when you cannot adjust the reverse proxy's idle timeout.
firstByteKeepalive.description: Injects downstream keepalive while waiting for the upstream first byte, preventing front reverse proxies from closing the apparently idle connection.
firstByteKeepalive.invalid: First-byte keepalive delay must be 0 or a positive integer number of seconds

streamDataTimeout.label: Upstream stream idle timeout
streamDataTimeout.hint: Stops an active streaming request when the upstream provider sends no SSE event for the configured number of seconds. Upstream ping events count as activity.
streamDataTimeout.description: Prevents a stalled upstream stream from being kept alive forever by downstream keepalive writes.
streamDataTimeout.envHint: can still provide the first deployment default.
streamDataTimeout.invalid: Stream idle timeout must be 0 or a positive integer number of seconds

upstreamHeaderTimeout.label: Upstream response header timeout
upstreamHeaderTimeout.hint: Caps how long each attempt waits for the upstream to send response headers. On expiry the attempt fails and the existing failover / automatic rescue rules continue; the body stream after headers arrive is unaffected.
upstreamHeaderTimeout.description: Prevents an upstream that accepts a request and then never answers from holding a single connection for the whole wait. This limits one attempt only, not the total length of automatic rescue.
upstreamHeaderTimeout.envHint: can still provide the first deployment default.
upstreamHeaderTimeout.invalid: Upstream response header timeout must be an integer between 0 and 86400 seconds

responsesSessionTTL.label: Responses session keep
responsesSessionTTL.hint: Remembers which channel and key own a previous_response_id, reducing broken continuations after restarts or route changes.
responsesSessionTTL.description: Only affects OpenAI Responses continuation routing memory. It does not change normal logs or billing.
responsesSessionTTL.invalid: Responses session keep time must be 0 or a positive integer number of seconds

sessionKeepTimeDefault.label: Global session-keep default
sessionKeepTimeDefault.hint: Fallback sticky window for groups whose own session-keep time is 0, so one client keeps hitting the same channel and key instead of scattering across upstreams and wasting prompt cache.
sessionKeepTimeDefault.description: Only a fallback: a group's own session-keep time still takes precedence. 0 disables the global default and keeps the legacy per-group-only behavior.
sessionKeepTimeDefault.invalid: Global session-keep default must be 0 or a positive integer number of seconds

firstTokenTimeOutDefault.label: Global first-token timeout default
firstTokenTimeOutDefault.hint: Fallback per-channel first-token timeout for groups whose own value is 0; if no first token arrives within this window the request moves on to the next channel. Streaming responses only.
firstTokenTimeOutDefault.description: Only a fallback: a group's own first-token timeout still takes precedence. 0 disables the global default and keeps the legacy per-group-only behavior.
firstTokenTimeOutDefault.invalid: Global first-token timeout default must be 0 or a positive integer number of seconds

routeModeOverride.label: Default channel order
routeModeOverride.hint: How channels are picked for new model routes and for models without a route. In order = always use the first channel and move to the next only when it fails (best upstream cache hits); Take turns = rotate across peer channels.
routeModeOverride.description: This is a default, not an override: routes whose order you set on the Plans page keep their own choice.
routeModeOverride.movedHint: Change it with 「Default channel order」 at the top of the Plans page.
routeModeOverride.defaultHint: Defaults to In order; switch to Take turns if needed. Routes with their own setting are unchanged.

poolDefaults.title: Model pool global defaults
poolDefaults.hint: Pool-wide routing defaults applied to every group: the route mode default only fills in for rules that have not chosen their own mode; the first-token and session-keep defaults only kick in when a group's own value is 0. A group's own configuration always takes precedence.

userRegistration.label: Allow Direct Registration
userRegistration.hint: When disabled, new users must enter an invite code. When enabled, users can register directly; an invite code still grants its quota or monthly card.

emailVerification.title: Email Verification on Registration
emailVerification.hint: When enabled, public registration requires an email and a 6-digit code sent to it. Configure the SMTP sender below.
emailVerification.passwordKeptPlaceholder: Already set, leave blank to keep current
emailVerification.sslHint: Enable for implicit TLS on port 465. Leave off for STARTTLS (e.g. port 587).
emailVerification.providerHint: Choose how verification codes are sent. HTTP API suits self-hosted services without SMTP (e.g. ClawEmail).

checkIn.title: User Daily Check-in

checkIn.randomRange: Random range (used when the mode is “Random range”)

upstreamError.title: Upstream Error Response

upstreamError.publicCodePlaceholder: Code shown to users, e.g. service_busy
upstreamError.customPlaceholder: Message shown to users when custom mode is selected

circuitBreaker.title: Circuit Breaker
circuitBreaker.hint: When a channel fails consecutively up to the threshold, circuit breaker trips. Cooldown grows exponentially up to the max cooldown

fingerprintProfile.title: Fingerprint Profiles
fingerprintProfile.description: Prepare multiple independent device fingerprints for different channels, so upstream keys behind different egress IPs present distinct devices instead of sharing one global fingerprint. Leave any field empty to fall back to the global default.
fingerprintProfile.empty: No fingerprint profiles yet. Click New to add one. Channels can still choose "Default (follow global)".
fingerprintProfile.dialogHint: Leave any field empty to fall back to the matching global default; only fill in the fields you want to differ on.
fingerprintProfile.genericUAHint: Unified User-Agent for non Claude/Codex channels (Gemini / plain OpenAI Chat), which emit no UA by default. Leave empty to keep current behaviour.

maxStorage.label: Log Storage Limit (GB)
maxStorage.hint: Estimated from request/response content; oldest logs are removed after the limit
maxStorage.cleanupNothing: Usage is within the limit; nothing to clean up.
maxStorage.cleanupVacuumFailed: Logs were trimmed to the limit, but disk space could not be reclaimed, so the file may stay the same size for now.

compact.label: Compact database
compact.tooltip: Deleting logs does not shrink the database file. Compacting returns the free space to disk (SQLite VACUUM). Requests may pause briefly while it runs; prefer a quiet time.
compact.hint: Requests may pause briefly while it runs
compact.confirm: Requests may pause briefly while the database is compacted. Compact now?
compact.busy: A compaction or space reclaim is already running, try again later
compact.fullWarning: The first compaction rebuilds the whole database file; the bigger it is the longer requests pause (minutes for GB-sized files). Run it at a quiet time

intervention.label: Automatic rescue for upstream errors
intervention.description: Automatic rescue retries the same user message on other channels once, at one retry per second, for at most 300 seconds. It runs at most once per new user message: once the rescue is exhausted, later requests carrying that same message are forwarded normally until one succeeds or a new user message arrives. Identical conversation histories cannot be told apart, so a repeated message shares the same rescue.

noBreaker.label: Automatic rescue window (sec)
noBreaker.hint: Default and maximum are both 300 seconds; 0 turns automatic rescue off. It applies to channels with the circuit breaker disabled, regardless of the switch above.

reclaim.label: Auto-reclaim disk space
reclaim.hint: Deleting logs does not shrink the file. When enabled, freed space is periodically returned to disk. VACUUM briefly locks the database; turn this off if it causes trouble.

upstreamRequestBody.label: Record the exact request sent upstream
upstreamRequestBody.hint: For troubleshooting. Saved as-is (API keys included) and uses more log storage

global.title: Credential Redaction
global.subtitle: Secrets are swapped for placeholders before reaching the upstream, and swapped back in the reply.
global.masterHint: When off, no channel is redacted.
global.noticeHint: Adds a short note before the first user message so the model understands the placeholders.
global.defaultFlagsHint: Detector set used when a channel has no override
global.scopeProtected: Protected: text and tool content from inbound Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages protocols only.
global.scopeUnprotected: Not protected: image/video generation, audio, file/form uploads, embeddings, raw endpoints, and native Gemini entrypoints bypass redaction.
global.scopeBypass: Chat attachments and identity/cache fields are not rewritten.
global.scopeWhyMedia: Why image/video/audio is not protected: the sensitive content lives in the pixels or the waveform (a password in a screenshot, say). Redaction only swaps text and cannot read an image, so wiring it in would look protected while still shipping the raw bytes.
global.scopeWhyEmbedding: Why embedding is not protected: it sends text and returns a vector, so the original words no longer exist and there is nothing to restore. Rewriting the input would also produce a different vector, making similarity search start matching unrelated documents. Leaving it untouched is the correct behaviour.

plans.title: Usable plans
plans.tip: Their API keys can only use these plans. New keys start on the default one.
plans.hint: New keys start on the default
plans.none: No plans yet — create one on the Plans page

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.desc: This can't be undone. It fails while they still own API keys — disable or delete those first.

password.title: Reset password for {name}
password.desc: Enter a new password; they'll use it next time they sign in.

drawer.roleTip: Admins can open the admin pages and aren't charged. The last admin can't be demoted.
drawer.canUseTip: When off they can't sign in and their keys stop working. The last admin can't be disabled.
drawer.balanceTip: Charged from here when there's no active card.
drawer.balanceTipAdmin: Admins aren't charged; this won't go down.
drawer.initialBalanceTip: Money they can use right away. Empty means 0.
drawer.cardTip: While active, calls only count against the card, not the balance; once today's amount is used up, calls stop until the reset. A daily amount of 0 or empty means no card.
drawer.expireTip: Expires at the end of this day.
drawer.clearTodayTip: Sets today's usage to 0 right away — no need to save.
drawer.badLimit: Per day must be 0 or more

redeem.title: Redeem codes
redeem.desc: Give a code to a user; they enter it on their page to add balance or start a card. Each code works once.

usage.costTip: Priced by model for all requests in this period. How much came from the card vs. the balance isn't recorded, so it isn't split.
usage.costTipAdmin: Admins aren't charged; this is the price only.
usage.dailyTip: Days follow the server's time zone.
usage.dailyAllTip: "All" only charts the last 30 days; the totals above cover all time.
usage.noModels: No models used in this period
usage.keysTip: Total cost is for the key's whole life and doesn't follow the period above.

alert.newIP: New IP {value} since {time}; {others} also used within {window}
alert.newClient: New client {value} since {time}; {others} also used within {window}
alert.hint: Could be a new network or device, or someone else using the key.

access.newPillTip: The new one named in the warning above
access.note: Recorded from the caller's IP and User-Agent (the real client IP when behind a trusted proxy). Entries not seen for {days} days are removed.

rule.off: No warnings (IPs and clients are still recorded)
rule.newIP: A never-seen IP within {window} while an old IP is still in use
rule.newClient: A never-seen client within {window} while the old one is still in use (version upgrades don't count)
rule.group32: IPv4 counted by full address; one IPv6 /64 counts as one
rule.group24: One IPv4 /24 counts as one; one IPv6 /64 counts as one
rule.footer: Warning only, requests are never blocked. Change it in Settings → Users & sign-up.

client.httpProxyTip: Behind a reverse proxy this is the proxy-to-Octopus hop; if the proxy sends X-HTTP-Version, the client's version is shown.
client.orderTip: Original order and casing as sent. Behind a proxy it is the order after the proxy.
client.orderUnknown: Original order not captured; sorted A–Z
client.orderUnknownTip: This connection's original order could not be captured (e.g. not HTTP/1.1); only the header names are listed.
client.headersTip: Values are kept only for non-secret headers; Authorization, x-api-key, Cookie etc. are stored by name only.
client.ja4hTip: HTTP fingerprint from request headers (FoxIO JA4H). Cookie values are not used; the last part is always 0.
client.noTLS: Octopus does not terminate HTTPS itself, so it cannot see the TLS fingerprint (JA3/JA4). Have the reverse proxy pass it in X-JA3 / X-JA4 headers (the proxy must be a trusted proxy) and it will show here.
client.note: Recorded from incoming requests; the same fingerprint from a new IP is not a new entry. Key and cookie values are never stored. Entries unseen for {days} days are removed; up to 100 per key.

unsaved.title: Not saved yet
unsaved.description: You have unsaved changes. Close anyway?

page.leadAdmin: What each key can use and how much it has spent.
page.leadUser: Copy a key into your client and you're set.

status.offTip: Turned off: every request with this key is rejected. Turn it back on to restore.
status.expiredTip: Past its expiry, so requests are rejected. Move the expiry later to restore.
status.used_upTip: Total spend went over this key's cap, so requests are rejected. Raise the cap or remove it to restore.

toolbar.searchAdmin: Name, user or last 4 of key

table.name: Name
table.spendHelp: Total spent by this key since it was created. Once it passes the cap, requests with this key are rejected. Only this key is affected, not the user's balance or card.
table.accessHelp: Which models and protocols the key can use. "All models" includes models added later.
table.allModelsTip: No model limit; models added later work too.
table.plansHelp: Plans this key can use. The filled one is the default; the X-Octopus-Plan header can pick another.
table.maskedTip: Only the last 4 characters are shown; use the button next to it to copy the full key

bulk.deleteDesc: Deleted keys stop working right away and their total spend is cleared. Request logs are kept.

delete.title: Delete "{name}"?
delete.desc: This key stops working right away and its total spend is cleared. Request logs are kept.

redeem.title: Redeem code
redeem.desc: Redeem balance or a card issued by an admin.

drawer.createHint: Copy the full key from the list once it's created.
drawer.name: Name
drawer.ownerTip: Whose key this is: spend is charged to their balance / card, and plans and selectable models follow them.
drawer.enabledHint: Turning it off blocks this key right away; turn it on to restore
drawer.capTip: Once this key's total spend since creation reaches this amount, its requests are rejected. Only this key is affected, not the user's balance or card.
drawer.expireTip: After this time, requests with this key are rejected. Uses your computer's time zone.
drawer.pastHint: This time has already passed; pick a later one before saving.
drawer.modelsTip: "All models" = no limit, including models added later. "Only these" = only the checked ones; new models are not added automatically.
drawer.modelsAllHint: No model limit; models added later work too.
drawer.modelsNone: This user's plans have no usable models right now
drawer.modelsOnlyHint: Lists the models currently usable under the owner's plans.
drawer.familiesTip: By request API: OpenAI-compatible (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses), Claude (/v1/messages), Gemini (/v1beta/models), Video (/v1/videos). Unchecked APIs are rejected.
drawer.plansTip: Plans this key can use. Requests use the default one; the X-Octopus-Plan header can switch to another selected plan.
drawer.plansTipUser: Plans an admin set for this key. The filled one is the default.
drawer.plansHint: Pick one or more; choose the default below
drawer.badCap: Spend cap must be a number
drawer.needModel: Pick at least one model, or switch back to "All models"
drawer.pastExpire: Expiry can't be in the past
drawer.createdHint: Copy it with the button next to the key in the list.
drawer.totalTip: Since creation; doesn't follow the range above. The cap uses this number.

guide.title: Setup guide
guide.desc: Pick your client and copy the snippet.

clientHint.curl: Try it right in a terminal.
clientHint.claude: Set the variables, then run claude.
clientHint.codex: Write the config file, set the variable, then run codex.
clientHint.gemini: Set the variables, then run gemini.
clientHint.video: Submit a job, then check it with the returned id.

claude.settings: Or save it in the settings file

video.status: Check progress (replace <id> with the returned id)

statusWarn.off: This key is disabled, so requests will be rejected; turn it on in its settings first.
statusWarn.expired: This key has expired, so requests will be rejected; move its expiry later first.
statusWarn.used_up: This key reached its spend cap, so requests will be rejected; raise the cap first.

guide.familyOff: This key doesn't allow the {family} protocol. Turn it on in the key's settings first.
guide.geminiNoPlan: Gemini CLI can't send custom headers, so it uses this key's default plan.
guide.modelsLimited: The model in the example is picked from this key's allowed models.
guide.modelsHint: The model names are examples; replace them with models you can use.

guest.lead: Temporary keys for guests: only the models you tick, expire on their own, no console access. Admins only.
guest.search: Search name, note, model or last 4
guest.emptyHint: Create one and send the guest the endpoint and key.

status.expiredTip: Past its expiry; requests are refused. Move the expiry later to restore.
status.used_upTip: Total spend is over the cap; requests are refused. Raise the cap to restore.
status.revokedTip: Revoked for good. Usage and logs are kept.

dialog.desc: The guest can only call the ticked models with this key. No console, no settings.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.expireTip: Stops working at that time. Max 365 days; never permanent.
dialog.capTip: The key stops once its total spend reaches this.
dialog.billing: Cost is booked to you (admin); nobody's balance is charged. Use the cap to limit it.
dialog.modelsTip: Only ticked models are allowed; new models are not added later. Pick at least one.
dialog.modelsHint: These are the models you can use right now.

err.pastExpire: Expiry can't be in the past

dialog.createdHint: Send the guest the endpoint and key. You can copy it from the list later too.

detail.billing: Booked to the admin, no balance charged; stops at the cap.

revoke.title: Revoke “{name}”?
revoke.desc: It stops working now and can't be turned back on. Usage, IPs and logs are kept.

delete.title: Delete “{name}”?
delete.desc: It stops working now and the key record is removed (request logs stay). To just stop it, use Revoke.
